messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: KV prefix cache hit-rate dropped for tenant `acme` in vpc `vpc-nyc-dedicated-03`. Metric: kv_prefix_hitrate went 0.94 -> 0.03 in 9m. Link: https://redwood/incident/1812005432

ops-bot: details -> policy=kvcache-prefix, pool=dp-acme-03, severity=page, evictions_spike=true

mike: oncall awake, ack. @sarah pull kv-proxy + memcache graphs. Any mitigation started?

sarah: grabbing graphs. Quick note: massive eviction bursts starting ~03:11 UTC. Cache miss rate at 0.99. Memcached evicted keys show repeated empty-segment keys like `tenant:acme:::session:abcd`.

juan: logs from kv-proxy (sanitized):
```
[03:10:59] WARN evict tenant=acme key=tenant:acme:::session:abcd size=1.6kb
[03:11:01] ERROR cache_lookup prefix_mismatch tenant=acme key=:::session:abcd
[03:11:05] WARN miss_rate 0.97 tenant=acme
```

kevin: likely templating regression from earlier config push. Two quick options: 1) disable prefix caching for acme only, 2) temporarily namespace-isolate memcache (map tenant -> namespace) — (2) is heavier.

april: prefer per-tenant toggle first, less blast radius. If we can flip via ops API we avoid memcache flush.

mike: show exact command you'll run and we'll stagger.

sarah: api call:
```
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP" \
  "https://ops-api.internal/pools/dp-acme-03/tenants/acme/cache/prefix/toggle?state=off"
```
I'll run on a single proxy first.

cse_emily: opened customer support note. Draft: "We're investigating transient errors affecting your VPC. We're applying a mitigation that may slightly increase latency; we'll follow up with timeline and RCA." Waiting for engineering ok.

mike: ok to send that. Keep it high level.

sarah: disabled prefix caching on replica-1 at 03:13:22 UTC. Misses drop locally. Rolling across replicas (serial, 20s). Watch for temporary miss spikes during roll.

kevin: rolling now. Also added a short traffic diversion to dp-acme-standby for 5m as extra safety:
```
opsctl route set --tenant acme --pool dp-acme-standby --duration 5m --reason "kvcache hit-rate collapse"
```

mike: handoff to sarah for next 30m to monitor and coordinate comms. I'll hold on root cause until stable.

sarah: accepted. @juan can you confirm which config change hit prod around 03:08? Need exact commit/id.

juan: found candidate push: config commit `cfg-2026-03-14-1667` applied at 03:07 with a template patch to prefix interpolation. Canary failed to respect tenant var for a subset of hosts (flag mis-evaluated) -> produced empty segment between colons.

kevin: that matches. Unexpected empty segment bypassed tenant namespace checks and crowded the shared cache with keys that hash to many slots.

april: next actions: rollback the bad config on dp-acme-03, add defensive check in template engine, expand canary gating.

mike: assign postmortem to sarah. Create L2 timeline + include exact RPCs and metric charts. Draft by EOD.

sarah: will. Follow-ups:
- PR for template guard (owner: juan) due by EOD tomorrow
- infra change to add per-tenant namespace enforcement in memcached (owner: kevin) due next week
- canary gating enhancement (owner: april) due in 48h

ops-bot: Metrics update 03:20 UTC -> pool dp-acme-03 prefix_hitrate recovered to 0.78 after per-tenant toggle + routing; 5xx dropped ~80% from peak.

cse_emily: customer updated: "Service restored; appreciate the quick remediation. Awaiting RCA." They requested ETA for permanent fix — offered 48h for template patch and weekly checkpoints.

sarah: marking mitigation complete. We'll not re-enable prefix caching until template patch lands and we confirm keys are sane. Postmortem will be posted to #postmortems.

ops-bot: incident resolved for customer-facing impact at 03:22 UTC. Case: INC-1812005432

(after action)

sarah: metrics: peak 5xx +380% from baseline, affected cluster traffic ~15% for 20m, avg latency bump +85ms on fallback. No SLA violation per preliminary calc but flagged.

mike: thanks team. reactions: :thumbsup: :coffee:
